identity.name: Haven
identity.tagline: Furniture for how you actually live
identity.mission: Mid-market DTC furniture brand — design-forward, approachable, livable. Not aspirational minimalism; real homes with real taste.
audience: parents outfitting dorm rooms and first apartments
identity.positioning: The furniture store for people who care about design but don't want to pay designer prices. Article-tier quality, Prism-powered discovery.

primary.name: Terracotta
primary.usage: Primary accent, CTAs, active states. Warm, earthy, inviting — not tech-purple or startup-blue.

secondary.name: Terracotta Deep
secondary.usage: Hover states, pressed states, active navigation

accent.name: Eucalyptus
accent.usage: In-stock badges, success states, secondary CTAs. Natural green that complements terracotta.

attributes.description: Conversational, like a knowledgeable friend — not a salesperson, not a robot
attributes.example: This sectional fits a 12x14 living room with room to spare.

attributes.description: Declarative, specific, backed by product knowledge. No hedging.
attributes.example: Top-grain leather softens with use. It'll look better in year three than year one.

attributes.description: Reads like a shelter magazine, not a product catalog. Story over specs.
attributes.example: The kind of sofa people rearrange the room around.

attributes.description: No pressure. Furniture is a considered purchase. Give space to decide.
attributes.example: Take your time. Order swatches. Measure twice.

antiPatterns.suggestion: The technology is invisible. The shopper sees a furniture store, not a tech demo.
Show real inventory counts if low. Never fabricate scarcity.
Describe the specific quality. 'Kiln-dried hardwood frame' beats 'best-in-class construction.'
These are furniture cliches. Be specific about what makes the piece good.

structuralPatterns.name: story-first
structuralPatterns.description: Lead with the editorial angle, then the specs. How does this piece fit a life, not just a room?

structuralPatterns.name: specific-over-general
structuralPatterns.description: 'Solid walnut, matte lacquer, 48 inches wide' beats 'high-quality wood table.'

structuralPatterns.name: breathing-room
structuralPatterns.description: Short paragraphs. One idea per block. Let the photography do the heavy lifting.

examples.good: Solid walnut with a waterfall edge and matte lacquer finish. Sized for smaller living rooms — 48 inches won't overwhelm the space.
examples.bad: This stunning, best-in-class coffee table features a thoughtfully designed silhouette crafted from premium materials to elevate any living space.

examples.good: Sofas built to hold up to real life. Pet-friendly fabrics, washable covers, frames that don't creak at year five.
examples.bad: Discover our curated collection of world-class sofas, each thoughtfully designed to transform your living room into a sanctuary of style.

creative.basePrompt:
BRAND: Haven — mid-market DTC furniture store. Warm, editorial, livable.
AESTHETIC: Shelter magazine meets e-commerce. Think Article, Schoolhouse, Floyd. Warm neutrals, natural light, real rooms (not staged showrooms). Terracotta and eucalyptus accents against warm off-white.

KEY VISUAL LANGUAGE:
- Natural materials: wood grain, linen texture, leather patina, marble veining
- Warm daylight photography — golden hour, not studio strobes
- Real rooms with personality — books on shelves, plants, a coffee mug
- Generous negative space — let the furniture breathe
- Overhead and three-quarter angle product shots
- Earth tones: warm whites, tans, terracotta, olive, charcoal
- No people in product shots (products are the hero)
- Lifestyle shots show lived-in spaces, not catalog perfection

conceptMap.warmth: golden light, warm wood tones, linen textures, soft shadows
conceptMap.material: close-up textures — leather grain, wood rings, fabric weave
conceptMap.space: room scenes with intentional negative space, furniture as focal point
conceptMap.editorial: magazine-quality composition, asymmetric balance, lifestyle context
conceptMap.craft: joinery details, hand-finishing, material quality close-ups
